verdict.benefit_premise: ALSO REFUTED on this case. The teleport count is 1 at every radius. The teleporting vehicle was stuck on the edge immediately BEFORE the closure, which is already inside 400 m, and SUMO reported 'No route found' -- it had passed a rerouter edge and still had no alternative. Reach was not its problem.
verdict.cost_premise: REFUTED. REROUTER_RADIUS_M = 400 exists because global rerouters were a bottleneck. Widening to 3000 m grows the rerouter from 58 to 4,979 edges (86x) with no wall-time increase at all; the 8.5 s at 400 m is first-run warm-up, the rest sit at 5.6-6.2 s.
verdict.limitation: ONE teleport on one edge with the deployed 2-day forecast demand is a thin sample. It is enough to refute the cost premise, which is a property of the network and SUMO, but not enough to prove reach never matters on a busier case.
verdict.recommendation: LEAVE THE CONSTANT AT 400 m. Widening is free but buys nothing measurable, and changing it would alter rerouting and therefore every scenario result, plus force another annual-plan regeneration, for no gain.
